topStory.headline: White House A.I. Framework Includes Workforce Development as Core Principle
topStory.summary:
The White House released its A.I. policy framework for Congress, outlining six guiding principles for lawmakers developing A.I. governance policies, according to WTAE. Among these principles is "educating Americans and developing an A.I.-ready workforce." The framework aims to preempt state-level regulations while ensuring "all Americans benefit from this technological revolution."

Workforce development sits alongside priorities like protecting children, safeguarding communities, and ensuring American A.I. dominance. The framework comes as President Trump signed an executive order in December blocking states from crafting their own A.I. regulations, arguing that inconsistent rules would hurt sector growth.

The framework does not specify what "A.I.-ready" means in practice, leaving room for interpretation about whether it refers to technical skills like coding and prompt engineering, or broader competencies like critical thinking about A.I.-generated content and understanding algorithmic bias.

stories.headline: White House A.I. Policy Aims to Block State Regulations
stories.summary: The White House released an A.I. policy framework that aims to preempt state rules while ensuring American industry can "innovate and thrive," according to Yahoo Finance. The move follows Trump's December executive order blocking states from crafting their own A.I. regulations.

stories.headline: Survey: Most Chattanooga Area Governments Lack A.I. Policies
stories.summary: A survey of 29 local agencies around Chattanooga found 20 have no A.I. policies, despite experts warning this creates security and privacy risks, according to Chattanooga Times Free Press. The few agencies with policies emphasize A.I. as a tool to help humans, not replace them, with explicit guidelines for appropriate use.

stories.headline: William Peace University Names New President
stories.summary: Jennifer Walsh will serve as the 13th president of the 700-student Raleigh institution William Peace University, according to the Charlotte Observer. She plans to grow enrollment through transfer students, military veterans, and new graduate programs while addressing the school's 32% four-year graduation rate.
